analysis: The method `unflattenMap` takes a `Map<String,String>` and builds a nested `Map<String,Object>`. It iterates over each entry, splits the key by '.', and uses `computeIfAbsent` to create intermediate maps (all `HashMap` instances). The `put` method is called on `currentMap`, which is always a `HashMap` (either the initial `result` or a newly created one via `computeIfAbsent`). The key is a `String` from splitting, never null. The value is a `String` from the map entry, which can be null, but `HashMap` permits null values. `HashMap.put` supports all operations, accepts any object types, allows null keys and values, and has no restrictions causing `IllegalArgumentException`. Therefore, none of the declared exceptions (`UnsupportedOperationException`, `ClassCastException`, `NullPointerException`, `IllegalArgumentException`) can occur from the `put` call in this context.
remark: All declared exceptions for `put` are avoided because the method is invoked on mutable `HashMap` instances, the key is always a non-null `String`, and the value (a `String`, possibly null) is accepted by `HashMap` without throwing any of these exceptions. `NullPointerException` could only occur if the map did not permit null values, but `HashMap` does. `ClassCastException` would require the key or value type to be incompatible, but `HashMap` accepts any `Object`. `UnsupportedOperationException` would require the map to be unmodifiable, which is not the case. `IllegalArgumentException` is not triggered by any property of the key or value.
